tools.name: list_bases
tools.description:
Lists all bases that you have access to in your Airtable account.
Use this to get the baseId of the base you want to use.
Favorited and recently viewed bases are generally more relevant.
If the response includes an offset, pass it in a subsequent call to retrieve the next page of results.

offset.description: Pagination cursor from a previous list_bases response. Pass this to retrieve the next page of results.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description:
Lists all workspaces the current user has access to, along with their permission level in each.
No dependencies. This is typically the first tool to call when you need a workspaceId.

offset.description: Pagination offset from the previous response. Pass this to retrieve the next page of results. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: search_bases
tools.description:
Searches for bases by name.
This is useful when you need to find a specific base quickly by a partial name-based match.
Returns bases sorted by their relevance score, as well as a recommended base ID and a hint on whether
we need to ask the user to explicitly select the base they want to use.

searchQuery.description:
The query to search for bases by name.
The search is case-insensitive and works with partial matches.
Examples: "projects", "issues", "customers"

tools.name: list_tables_for_base

sort.description:
A list of sort objects that specifies how the records will be ordered.
Each sort object must have a fieldId key specifying the field to sort on (ID or name), and an optional direction key that is either "asc" or "desc".
The default direction is "asc".
Records are sorted by the first sort object first, then by the second sort object for records that have the same value for the first sort, and so on.
Example sort by a single field in descending order: [{"fieldId": "Status", "direction": "desc"}]
Example sort by two fields, first ascending then descending: [{"fieldId": "Priority", "direction": "asc"}, {"fieldId": "Created", "direction": "desc"}]

Example: "recZOTa3BDHxlJNzf".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs
To get recordId, use the list_records_for_table tool or display_records_for_table tools.

operator.description:
The operator to use to combine the operands (filter conditions).
Acceptable values are 'and' and 'or'.
The default operator is 'and'.

The comparison operator for this filter condition, applied to the operands.
Acceptable values are =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isWithin, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, contains, doesNotContain, filename, fileType, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
For singleSelect and singleCollaborator fields, use =, !=, isAnyOf, or isNoneOf.
For multipleSelects and multipleCollaborators fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, or doesNotContain.
For multipleRecordLinks (linked record) fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, isNoneOf, contains, or doesNotContain.

operands.description:
The operands (arguments) to the comparison operator.
The first operand must be a field ID. Example: "fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM". Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
The second operand depends on the operator and field type:
    - isEmpty, isNotEmpty: No second operand (use a single-element array with just the field ID).
    - =, !=, contains, doesNotContain: A string for text fields, a number for number fields, a boolean for checkbox fields.
    - <, >, <=, >=: A number.
    - For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields: The second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selABCDEFGHIJKLM") obtained from get_table_schema, not the choice
    name.
    - hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, doesNotContain: An array of strings (e.g., choice IDs for select fields, collaborator IDs for collaborator fields, record IDs for multipleRecordLinks fields).
    - For multipleRecordLinks (linked record) fields with =, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, or isNoneOf: The second operand must be an array of record IDs (e.g., ["recABCDEFGHIJKLM"]), not record display names or a plain string. Unlike other field types, = takes an array here. Use contains/doesNotContain with a string to match by record display name instead.
    - For date/datetime fields with =, !=, <, >, <=, >=: The second operand is a date value object, e.g. {"mode": "today", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "exactDate",
    "exactDate": "2024-01-15", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, or {"mode": "daysAgo", "numberOfDays": 7, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - isWithin (date fields only): The second operand is a date range object, e.g. {"mode": "pastWeek", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "pastNumberOfDays", "numberOfDays":
    30, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - filename: A string to match against attachment filenames.
    - fileType: Either "image" or "text".
For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, the second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selet1KAKDTOhXQJk") obtained from get_table_schema.

matchGroupsByMembership.description:
Only set this when operand is a collaborator field.
When true, groups are matched by their individual members.
When false, groups are matched by their literal group ID.

Whether end users can edit, create, or delete records through this element. Editability is
stored per table, and tables can have differing values (returned per table by
describe_custom_element); this input overwrites EVERY table's editability
with the single value provided — it cannot target individual tables. Omit to leave every
table's editability unchanged, including any per-table differences. Tables newly added to
the element's config are read-only by default.

key.description: The string key declared for useCustomProperties in the custom element source code.

value.description: The value to set. For table and field properties, use the ID rather than the name.

customPropertyValues.description:
Custom property values to set on the element. Keys correspond to useCustomProperties hooks
in the source code. Only the keys you include are changed. Omit to leave all custom properties
unchanged.

visibleFieldIds.description:
Field IDs visible to the Custom Element for this table. This must be provided for new
            custom elements, or when adding a table to an existing custom element's config. Otherwise,
            omit to leave the table's visible fields unchanged.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

operator.description:
The operator to use to combine the operands (filter conditions).
Acceptable values are 'and' and 'or'.
The default operator is 'and'.

The comparison operator for this filter condition, applied to the operands.
Acceptable values are =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isWithin, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, contains, doesNotContain, filename, fileType, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
For singleSelect and singleCollaborator fields, use =, !=, isAnyOf, or isNoneOf.
For multipleSelects and multipleCollaborators fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, or doesNotContain.
For multipleRecordLinks (linked record) fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, isNoneOf, contains, or doesNotContain.

operands.description:
The operands (arguments) to the comparison operator.
The first operand must be a field ID. Example: "fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM". Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
The second operand depends on the operator and field type:
    - isEmpty, isNotEmpty: No second operand (use a single-element array with just the field ID).
    - =, !=, contains, doesNotContain: A string for text fields, a number for number fields, a boolean for checkbox fields.
    - <, >, <=, >=: A number.
    - For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields: The second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selABCDEFGHIJKLM") obtained from get_table_schema, not the choice
    name.
    - hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, doesNotContain: An array of strings (e.g., choice IDs for select fields, collaborator IDs for collaborator fields, record IDs for multipleRecordLinks fields).
    - For multipleRecordLinks (linked record) fields with =, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, or isNoneOf: The second operand must be an array of record IDs (e.g., ["recABCDEFGHIJKLM"]), not record display names or a plain string. Unlike other field types, = takes an array here. Use contains/doesNotContain with a string to match by record display name instead.
    - For date/datetime fields with =, !=, <, >, <=, >=: The second operand is a date value object, e.g. {"mode": "today", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "exactDate",
    "exactDate": "2024-01-15", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, or {"mode": "daysAgo", "numberOfDays": 7, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - isWithin (date fields only): The second operand is a date range object, e.g. {"mode": "pastWeek", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "pastNumberOfDays", "numberOfDays":
    30, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - filename: A string to match against attachment filenames.
    - fileType: Either "image" or "text".
For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, the second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selet1KAKDTOhXQJk") obtained from get_table_schema.

matchGroupsByMembership.description:
Only set this when operand is a collaborator field.
When true, groups are matched by their individual members.
When false, groups are matched by their literal group ID.

operands.description:
A list of filter conditions to apply to the records. These are combined using the top-level operator (default "and").
Each filter condition must have an "operator" key (the comparison operator, e.g. "=", "contains", "isEmpty", etc) and an "operands" key (an array where
the first element is a field ID and the optional second element is the value to compare against).
Example: [{"operator": "contains", "operands": ["fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM", "apple"]}]

sorts.description:
Sort order for the records exposed from this table to the custom element.
Omit to leave sorts unchanged; pass an empty array to clear them.

configByTableId.description:
Per-table configuration changes to apply, keyed by table ID. Configs passed for tables already
in the element's config will only have defined properties updated. New tables will be added
to the element with the provided config. Omitted tables will be left unchanged - this tool
currently cannot remove tables from the element.
Must start with "tbl" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG".
Do not substitute user-facing names for tableId.
To get tableId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.
